paragraphs.title: God Is Present in Judgment and Demands Justice

answers: In the congregation of the mighty
Among the nations
In the house of the wicked
easy.explanation: Psalm 82:1 says, “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty.”
easy.q: Where does God stand according to verse 1?

answers: The poor
The gods
The fatherless
easy.explanation: The verse says that God “judgeth among the gods.”
easy.q: Whom does God judge among according to verse 1?

answers: Accepting the persons of the wicked
Defending the needy
Judging with perfect justice
easy.explanation: The verse asks why they “judge unjustly” and “accept the persons of the wicked.”
easy.q: What are the judges accused of doing in verse 2?

answers: To favor or show partiality toward wicked people
To rescue the wicked from danger
To punish the wicked fairly
medium.explanation: The phrase describes showing favoritism to the wicked instead of judging impartially.
medium.q: What does “accept the persons of the wicked” mean in this context?

answers: The injustice has been continuing
The judgment has already ended
The judges have never acted
medium.explanation: “How long” suggests that the unjust conduct has persisted and must stop.
medium.q: What does the question “How long” suggest about the judges’ actions?

answers: It shows that the judges are accountable for their decisions
It proves that justice is unnecessary
It excuses the judges from responsibility
medium.explanation: Because God is present in the judgment, the judges’ injustice is exposed as a serious offense.
medium.q: Why is God’s presence among the judges important to the message?

answers: God is present in judgment, but the judges act unjustly
God is absent, but the judges act perfectly
The wicked judge God, and the poor rule the earth
challenge.explanation: Verse 1 presents God as present in the assembly, while verse 2 condemns the judges’ injustice.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between verses 1 and 2?

answers: It places the judges under divine examination
It removes all responsibility from the judges
It identifies the judges as immortal beings
challenge.explanation: The judges are portrayed as standing before God and therefore subject to His scrutiny.
challenge.q: How does the phrase “among the gods” affect the authority of the judgment?

answers: That judgment should be just and impartial
That the wicked should receive special treatment
That all judgment should be abandoned
challenge.explanation: The rebuke calls for an end to unjust judgment and favoritism toward the wicked.
challenge.q: What is the central demand of these verses?

short_answers.question: In one short phrase, describe the main problem condemned in verses 1–2.
short_answers.answer: Unjust judgment and favoritism toward the wicked.
short_answers.explanation: The judges are condemned for judging unjustly and accepting the persons of the wicked.

paragraphs.title: The Judges’ Duty to Protect the Helpless

answers: The poor and fatherless
The wicked and powerful
The rulers of the nations
easy.explanation: Verse 3 commands, “Defend the poor and fatherless.”
easy.q: Whom are the judges commanded to defend?

answers: Do justice to them
Ignore them
Deliver them to the wicked
easy.explanation: The verse says to “do justice to the afflicted and needy.”
easy.q: What are the judges told to do for the afflicted and needy?

answers: The hand of the wicked
The hand of the fatherless
The hand of the judges
easy.explanation: Verse 4 commands the judges to rid the poor and needy “out of the hand of the wicked.”
easy.q: From whose hand should the poor and needy be rescued?

answers: Suffering or oppressed
Wealthy and powerful
Proud and rebellious
medium.explanation: The afflicted are people who are suffering or being oppressed and therefore need justice.
medium.q: What does the word “afflicted” most nearly mean in verse 3?

answers: They walk on in darkness
They become wise rulers
They rescue the needy
medium.explanation: Verse 5 says, “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.”
medium.q: What happens when the people described in verse 5 lack understanding?

answers: The foundations of society have become unstable
The earth has been physically created again
The wicked have completely disappeared
medium.explanation: The expression pictures social and moral disorder caused by failed judgment.
medium.q: What does “all the foundations of the earth are out of course” communicate?

answers: Failure to protect the weak undermines the foundations of society
Protecting the weak makes justice unnecessary
The weak are responsible for the disorder
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the duty to protect the vulnerable to the warning that the foundations of the earth are out of course.
challenge.q: What connection do these verses make between protecting the weak and preserving society?

answers: To emphasize the broad responsibility to defend vulnerable people
To limit justice to one particular group
To identify the judges as helpless
challenge.explanation: The different descriptions reinforce the judges’ duty to protect all kinds of vulnerable people.
challenge.q: Why are several groups mentioned—poor, fatherless, afflicted, and needy?

answers: Failure to understand and practice justice leads to social disorder
Rescuing the needy causes the wicked to rule
The poor create darkness by refusing judgment
challenge.explanation: When justice is neglected and truth is not understood, the result is darkness and instability.
challenge.q: What is the main cause-and-effect relationship in verses 3–5?

short_answers.question: In one short sentence, state the judges’ responsibility in verses 3–4.
short_answers.answer: They must defend the vulnerable and rescue them from the wicked.
short_answers.explanation: The judges are commanded to defend the poor and fatherless, do justice to the afflicted and needy, and deliver them from the wicked.

paragraphs.title: The Failure of the Judges and the Appeal to God

answers: Gods and children of the most High
Poor and fatherless
Wicked and afflicted
easy.explanation: God says, “Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”
easy.q: What does God call the judges in verse 6?

answers: They shall die like men
They shall live forever
They shall inherit all nations
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “Ye shall die like men.”
easy.q: What will happen to the judges according to verse 7?

answers: Arise and judge the earth
Hide the earth
Favor the wicked
easy.explanation: The psalmist prays, “Arise, O God, judge the earth.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do in verse 8?

answers: To possess or hold authority over all nations
To abandon all nations
To flee from all nations
medium.explanation: In this context, “inherit” expresses God’s possession and sovereign authority over all nations.
medium.q: What does “inherit all nations” mean in verse 8?

answers: To show that their authority and status are not eternal
To prove that they were never judges
To show that they do not need God
medium.explanation: Their elevated title does not make them immortal; they remain mortal human beings.
medium.q: Why does the psalm emphasize that the judges will die like men?

answers: The judges are given an exalted title, their mortality is exposed, and the psalmist appeals to God
The wicked are rescued, the poor disappear, and the earth is destroyed
The nations vanish, the judges become immortal, and the psalmist remains silent
medium.explanation: The passage first describes the judges as gods, then declares their mortality, and finally calls on God to judge the earth.
medium.q: What is the sequence of ideas in verses 6–8?

answers: They are expected to represent divine authority, yet they are mortal human beings
They are poor, yet they control all nations
They are wicked, yet they cannot be judged
challenge.explanation: The judges receive an exalted designation but are reminded that they will die like men.
challenge.q: What central tension is presented concerning the judges?

answers: The psalmist asks God Himself to bring true judgment
The psalmist wants judgment to be abolished
The psalmist wants the wicked to receive special treatment
challenge.explanation: After human judges fail, the psalmist turns to God as the ultimate righteous Judge.
challenge.q: Why does the appeal to God follow the description of the judges’ failure?

answers: God’s judgment and authority extend over the whole earth
The judges rule only over one small place
The psalmist is concerned only with the poor
challenge.explanation: The closing verse expands the scope from human judges to God’s authority over all nations.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the movement from the judges to “all nations”?

short_answers.question: In one short sentence, explain why the psalmist calls on God in verse 8.
short_answers.answer: Because human judges have failed, the psalmist asks God to arise and judge the earth.
short_answers.explanation: The appeal to God follows the judges’ failure and recognizes God as the ultimate source of righteous judgment.
